why: The finding is real. The sentence is in theories/becoming/chapters/CIVILIZATION-THOUGHT-AND-BECOMING.md at line 239, not in the 中华本 itself, and the find occurs only once there. In work/names-checked.json, which is the file build_tables.py counts from, 步 (古) has a quotation, 「不積跬步」 found at RU2-S-XZ01, and 亡 (古) has 「死而不亡者寿」 found at YD-LAO-BASE. The appendix 名表 of THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING-ZHONGHUA.md shows the same two quotations at lines 3590 and 3667. So two of the four examples given for 'names with no recorded quotation' do have one. 聚, 散, 衡 and 耗 are all 古 with no quotations ("引": "—"). 相續 is a 复 with no quotation either. I changed the reviewer's set to 聚、散、衡、相续 so the examples include a 复 as well as 古 names, matching '古名或复名'. In prose the name is written in simplified script (繁体立名，简体行文), and 相续 appears in the 中华本.
